claims.claim: Born Rosa Gorelick on December 3, 1893, in Shchedrin near Babruysk, to Solomon (a rabbi) and Chasya Gorelick (grocery store operator), one of eight children
Other accounts describe her birthplace as near Minsk, in 1893
Began working in her mother's grocery store as a child
Married Isadore Blumkin in 1913; arrival in the United States given as 1916
Arrival given as 1917, in Seattle; then Fort Dodge, Iowa; moved to Omaha in 1919 and started a used clothing store
Route: train across Siberia, past a border guard into China, boat to Japan, ship to Seattle
Husband emigrated before her; he died in 1950; she had four children
Founded Nebraska Furniture Mart in 1937 at age 44 with $500 (Buffett letter excerpt: started the business at 44 with $500)
Store opened in the basement of her husband's store
The $500 was borrowed from her brother
Manufacturers and banks initially refused her; son Louie and grandsons Ron and Irv worked in the business; store opened 1937
Buffett's 1984 letter: Berkshire purchased 90 percent, no audit, check for $55 million
Other sources: 90 percent for $60 million in 1983

A later Buffett letter says the family sold 80 percent in 1983; she continued as chairman and ran the carpet operation; left in 1989 over a managerial disagreement and opened her own operation next door; later sold building and land to NFM and signed a non-compete agreement
Retired at 95 in 1989; competing store called Mrs. B's Clearance and Factory Outlet became the third largest carpet outlet in Omaha; no non-compete had been signed in 1983
Buffett acquired the outlet in 1992
Buffett letters: 100th birthday on December 3 (1993 letter); she is 103 and still working (1996 letter)
Died August 9, 1998, in Omaha, aged 104; honorary degrees from New York University and Creighton University; Rose Blumkin Performing Arts Center named for her
More than 1,000 attended her funeral; $1 million gift to a Jewish nursing home in 1981
Listed in the American Home Furnishings Hall of Fame
Buffett's 1984 letter: Mrs. B boils it down to 'sell cheap and tell the truth'

quotes.text: Sell cheap and tell the truth.
quotes.source: Attributed to her by Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway Chairman's Letter, 1984 (read in a third-party reproduction of the letter, also excerpted at moneylemma.com)

uncertain: Source access: berkshirehathaway.com/letters returned a bot-check redirect, nfm.com returned Access Denied, and nytimes.com could not be fetched. Buffett letter text was read only through third-party reproductions and excerpts (focusonrisksv.substack.com, moneylemma.com). The NYT obituary and NFM history page were not read. Re-check the letter quotes against the official PDFs before publishing.

The quotes were confirmed through a summarizing fetch tool, not by reading raw page text. The two UPI quotes appear as adjacent sentences in the tool output; confirm they are one continuous quote. Verify exact wording and capitalization of all three before publishing (in Buffett's letter the motto is lower case inside a parenthetical).

Birth date: every source fetched gives December 3, 1893, and Buffett's 1993 letter dates her 100th birthday to December 3. The task mentions a birth date dispute; no competing date was found in the pages fetched, so none is reported.
Birthplace: Wikipedia says Shchedrin near Babruysk; UPI, J Weekly and others say Minsk or a village near Minsk.

Arrival year: 1917 (Wikipedia, Hall of Fame, Omaha Exploration) versus 1916 (J Weekly). J Weekly also says she arrived with the equivalent of $66. One Buffett excerpt says she was 23 when she left Russia.

Starting sum: $500 in all sources; whether it was borrowed from her brother (Wikipedia NFM, J Weekly, Hall of Fame says borrowed) or simply her own investment is not settled. Omaha Exploration says she opened with a brother-in-law, Louis Friedman; left out.
Founding year: 1937 in nearly all sources; the Wikipedia article on her also contains 1933.

1983 sale terms: 90 percent for $55 million (Buffett 1984 letter excerpt, J Weekly, Omaha Exploration), 90 percent for $60 million (Wikipedia, UPI 1984), 80 percent (later Buffett letter excerpt, Wikipedia NFM article).

Death date: Wikipedia and J Weekly give August 9, 1998 (a Sunday). A search snippet of the NYT obituary says she died 'on Friday', which would be August 7. Not resolved because the NYT page could not be fetched.

The year of the Buffett letter reporting her return and the non-compete is labeled 1989 on the excerpt page, but the text says she was 99, which points to the 1992 letter. The profile dates the sale of her store to 1992 following Wikipedia. A $4.94 million price for that sale appeared only in a search snippet and was left out.

Husband's name is spelled Isadore, Isidore or Izya in different sources. Hall of Fame induction year not found. 'Worked until 103' rests on Buffett's 1996 letter excerpt; yearsActive end of 1997 is an approximation.
